page: Vultr voc-m-8c-64gb-800s-amd is an instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core. The system architecture is x86_64, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz with a 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled and consists of an 800 GB NVMe SSD. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not feature a GPU.

Benchmark data indicates a contrast between single-core and multi-core execution. The single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, ranks in the top tier (top 10%), whereas multi-core CPU performance falls into the average category. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks show strong performance in the top 25% for both read and write operations, and the PassMark memory score is similarly positioned in the top 25%. However, computational limits are visible in complex workloads; while text generation for a 7B LLM model achieves average speeds, prompt processing for the same model drops to the bottom 25%.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers a high memory allocation relative to its compute cores, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores, 64.0 GB of RAM, and 800 GB of local NVMe storage makes this configuration suitable for database hosting, redis caching, memory-intensive web serving, and moderate data processing tasks.
